title: Blackheath & Lee
intro: A Georgian village on an open heath, with Greenwich Park and the river a short walk away and the gardens of Lee to the south.

items.name: Blackheath and All Saints'
items.blurb: The wide open heath that gives the village its name, with the spire of All Saints' church standing alone on the grass.
items.tip: Come in spring for the kite-flying and the views across London.

items.name: Greenwich Park
items.blurb: A royal park on a hill, home to the Royal Observatory, with a famous view over the Queen's House and the river to Canary Wharf.
items.tip: Enter through the gate on the Blackheath side and walk to the Observatory for the view.

items.name: The Paragon
items.blurb: A crescent of grand Georgian houses linked by colonnades, built around 1800 and one of the finest set pieces in south London.
items.tip: It's a private road, but the crescent is best seen from South Row.

items.name: Blackheath Village
items.blurb: The village centre around Tranquil Vale, with independent shops, cafés and a Sunday farmers' market by the station.
items.tip: The Sunday farmers' market is the best time to visit.

items.name: Ranger's House
items.blurb: An 18th-century villa on the edge of Greenwich Park, run by English Heritage, with the Wernher Collection of art and jewels inside.
items.tip: Check opening days before you go: it is not open every day.

items.name: Eltham Palace
items.blurb: A medieval royal palace with a great hall, joined in the 1930s to an Art Deco house, set in moated gardens.
items.tip: The Art Deco entrance hall is the highlight; book ahead.
